# Fernando Landero — landerox.com

> Fernando Landero is an independent Senior Consultant & Engineer in Cloud,
> Data & AI Platforms, with over 15 years in technology (the last 7 on cloud
> and data platforms). He designs architectures, writes production code and
> automates platforms on Google Cloud (GCP), AWS and private cloud: Terraform
> and policy-checked infrastructure, GKE/Kubernetes, batch and streaming
> pipelines with Apache Spark, BigQuery, dbt and Airflow, and AI workflows
> with RAG retrieval, agent orchestration and observability (OpenTelemetry,
> Langfuse). Recent work: banking and finance, retail and energy.

Bilingual site: English at https://landerox.com/, Spanish at
https://landerox.com/es/.

## Pages

- [Home](https://landerox.com/): introduction, proof, core expertise and
  contact
- [About](https://landerox.com/about/): profile, focus areas, experience
- [Tech Stack](https://landerox.com/stack/): production tools and research candidates
- [Technical Glossary](https://landerox.com/glossary/): 59 bilingual terms
  with stable anchors, related concepts, examples and primary sources
- [Collaboration & Contact](https://landerox.com/collaboration/): typical
  requests, engagements, time zones, scheduling
- [Projects](https://landerox.com/projects/): open-source software, production
  blueprints, research labs, the tech radar and interactive tools
- [Open Source](https://landerox.com/projects/open-source/): ZDX, an MIT-licensed
  fzf-powered developer suite for Zsh (251 commands, 15 suites,
  https://github.com/landerox/zdx-suite), and this site's audited pipeline
- [Research Labs](https://landerox.com/projects/labs/): internal project status,
  evaluation contracts and research baselines
- [Interactive Tools](https://landerox.com/projects/tools/): reproducible failure-policy
  comparisons, memory scenarios, SQL stages, SLO/error budgets, schema diffs and
  a lakehouse table-file planner; shareable scenario links, no remote execution
- [Blog](https://landerox.com/blog/): concise explanations and practical
  technology comparisons with results, dated editorial 1–5 ratings per tool
  and primary sources
- [Object Storage](https://landerox.com/blog/object-storage/): open-source
  server and gateway choices by workload, release status, S3 limits and recovery
- [Workflow Orchestrators](https://landerox.com/blog/workflow-orchestrators/):
  Airflow, Dagster and alternatives by execution model, licensing and recovery
- [OLAP Databases](https://landerox.com/blog/olap-databases/): distributed,
  embedded and PostgreSQL options, including AGPL candidates
- [Vector Databases](https://landerox.com/blog/vector-databases/): Qdrant and
  alternatives by filtered retrieval, license, deployment and evaluation
- [Graph Databases](https://landerox.com/blog/graph-databases/): Neo4j Community,
  AGE and alternatives by graph model, edition, deployment and recovery
- [Transformation](https://landerox.com/blog/data-transformation/): dbt Core,
  SQLMesh, Dataform and Bruin by model lifecycle and deployment responsibility
- [BI and Visualization](https://landerox.com/blog/business-intelligence/):
  Superset, Metabase and alternatives by reader workflow and permissions
- [Lakehouse Table Formats](https://landerox.com/blog/lakehouse-table-formats/):
  Iceberg, Delta, Hudi and DuckLake; table, catalog and engine boundaries
- [Observability](https://landerox.com/blog/observability/): metrics, logs,
  traces, profiles, collectors and dashboards compared by architectural role
- [Production Blueprints](https://landerox.com/projects/blueprints/): upstream
  foundations, workload fit, shared Ops responsibilities, UX/UI principles
  and production readiness gates
- [Tech Radar](https://landerox.com/projects/explorations/): dated upstream
  research and adoption conditions, not published internal benchmark results

The technical glossary contains 36 authored bilingual definitions, practical
examples, caveats and primary-source links. Static pages are available in both
locales, with local typo-tolerant filtering and links between terms. It does not
call an AI service and does not repeat the site's biography or project pages.
